headline: Hormuz shock and Treasury scare usher in a decade of financial repression

events: Israel-Iran exchange escalates into tanker strikes; Strait of Hormuz traffic disrupted for six weeks, Brent peaks near $135
French budget impasse triggers OAT-Bund spread blowout; ECB activates TPI for the first time
US raises tariffs on Chinese and Vietnamese goods again; China tightens rare-earth and gallium export licensing
Record Northern Hemisphere heat and Rhine low water cut European industrial output
G20 inflation re-accelerates past 5%; Fed pauses cuts and hikes once
Weak 30-year US Treasury auction amid election-year deficit fights sends 10-year yield above 6%; Fed launches 'market functioning' purchases and caps long yields informally
AI equity correction of ~40% after hyperscalers cut capex guidance; credit stress in private-credit funds financing data centres
Global recession: world growth ~0.4%, unemployment climbs toward 6.8%
G20 inflation peaks at 7.2% on energy, food and tariff pass-through
Pakistan and Egypt default; IMF resources stretched as US withholds new quota funding
Failed South Asian monsoon and Sahel drought drive grain prices up 45%; India bans rice exports
Kenya, Ghana (again), Bolivia and Argentina enter debt crises; Common Framework collapses into ad-hoc bilateral deals with China and Gulf lenders
UK and Italy face bond-market episodes; Bank of England reverses QT
Japan's BoJ abandons yield normalisation after JGB volatility spike, yen weakens past 190
Mass protests over food and fuel in Lagos, Dhaka, Cairo and Paris; populist governments elected in two G7 states
China declares customs 'quarantine' around Kinmen and Matsu; US and Japan respond with naval escorts and chip export embargo, ten-day semiconductor panic
Western sanctions on Chinese banks fragment payments; BRICS settlement network handles a quarter of Global South trade
Armed conflict breaks out in the Horn of Africa over Nile water and Red Sea ports
Energy-security drive accelerates solar and battery build-out in Europe, India and China; coal also rebounds in Asia
AI adoption broadens as firms automate back-office functions to cut costs; white-collar layoffs spark backlash
Weak recovery (~2.3% world growth) under financial repression: capped yields, mandated bank bond holdings, inflation ~4%
US debt reaches 141% of GDP; Congress passes partial entitlement trims and a tariff-funded deficit package
Third Category-5 hurricane in two years strikes the US Gulf Coast; reinsurers withdraw from Florida and Louisiana
EU issues joint defence and energy bonds at scale, narrowing peripheral spreads
Warming reaches ~1.62C; COP talks stall on finance as donor aid budgets shrink further

winners: Gulf and Norwegian energy exporters and sovereign funds
Owners of real assets and AI-platform incumbents with pricing power
losers: Import-dependent low-income countries in Africa and South Asia
Young renters and pensioners on fixed nominal incomes
bullets: Advanced economies live under de facto financial repression: central banks cap long yields and inflation of ~4% quietly erodes debt
Global public debt has climbed to ~112% of GDP after a 2028 recession, energy subsidies and defence spending
Nine sovereign debt crises, mostly in frontier and lower-middle-income economies, leave the IMF overstretched and China and Gulf states as key creditors
Trade is split into US-aligned and China-aligned blocs with separate chip, payments and standards regimes; the Kinmen quarantine hardened the divide
Energy insecurity paradoxically speeds solar and storage (renewables ~41% of electricity) while Asian coal use also rebounds
AI spreads to ~31% of firms mainly as a cost-cutting tool, displacing ~38 million jobs and fuelling white-collar anxiety
Food and fuel protests and populist electoral swings keep unrest high and institutional trust near record lows
Climate disasters at ~1.6C are making whole regions uninsurable and pushing migration from the Sahel and South Asia
wildcard: China's customs quarantine of Kinmen and Matsu in 2030 briefly froze advanced-chip shipments worldwide
image_description: In a sweltering 2031 Cairo evening, a queue of commuters with phone-based ration codes waits beneath a flickering solar-powered streetlight outside a subsidised bread kiosk, while a delivery drone hums overhead.
